Commander. Naval Base San Diego. HIGH OPSEC exposure identified across multiple vectors.

HIGH — Satellite imaging. Sentinel-1A pass in 5.4 hours at 19 degrees elevation. 15 passes within the next 24 hours. Any outdoor activity or equipment movement will be commercially visible, compromising operational secrecy.

MODERATE — Aircraft. Two military flights logged on public ADS-B trackers in the last 7 days. No consistent military pattern detected. However, peak activity between 0300 and 0700 could indicate vulnerability during early morning operations.

MINIMAL — Fitness activity. No Strava heatmap data available. No exposure from personnel movement patterns.

Composite exposure score: 33 out of 100. Risk level: MEDIUM.

Recommended actions. One: reschedule all outdoor activities to avoid satellite pass windows, especially within the next 24 hours. Two: increase monitoring of ADS-B feeds for any emerging patterns during peak hours. Three: maintain current OPSEC protocols for personal fitness tracking.
